analysis.evidence: Enosh is the subject of וַיְחִי. The verse counts the 815 years he lived after fathering Kenan.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־ and shortened verb form יְחִי.
analysis.sense: live for a stated length of time

analysis.evidence: אֱנוֹשׁ is the named subject of וַיְחִי ‘he lived’. The phrase אַחֲרֵי הוֹלִידוֹ אֶת קֵינָן ‘after he fathered Kenan’ identifies him as Kenan’s father in the genealogy.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אַחֲרֵי introduces הוֹלִידוֹ אֶת קֵינָן, “his fathering Kenan.” Enosh lived 815 years after that event.
analysis.morphology: Preposition in the plural construct form אַחֲרֵי, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: After אַחֲרֵי “after,” the suffix וֹ identifies Enosh as the father, and אֶת marks Kenan as the direct object. The phrase means “after he fathered Kenan.”
analysis.morphology: Hiphil infinitive construct with a third-person masculine singular subject suffix

analysis.evidence: In אַחֲרֵי הוֹלִידוֹ אֶת קֵינָן, “after he fathered Kenan,” אֶת marks the proper name קֵינָן as the direct object of הוֹלִידוֹ. Enosh is the father and Kenan is the child he fathered.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle without prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for Kenan with its etymology left open pending evidence.
draft.definition: Kenan, the son of Enosh named in the genealogy of Genesis 5.
draft.evidence: Genesis 5:10 names Kenan as the child Enosh had fathered. The verse gives no explanation of the name’s meaning.

analysis.evidence: In אַחֲרֵי הוֹלִידוֹ אֶת קֵינָן, “after he fathered Kenan,” אֶת marks קֵינָן as the direct object of “fathered.” Enosh is the father, and Kenan is the child.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name in the absolute state, with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: The personal name of Enosh’s son.

analysis.evidence: In חֲמֵשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה, חֲמֵשׁ supplies the five in “fifteen years.” The verse adds these fifteen years to eight hundred to give the time Enosh lived after fathering Kenan.
analysis.morphology: Cardinal numeral, feminine singular absolute, in the compound חֲמֵשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה.

analysis.evidence: In חֲמֵשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה, “fifteen years,” עֶשְׂרֵה supplies the ten and חֲמֵשׁ supplies the five. The feminine form agrees with שָׁנָה, “year.”
analysis.sense: ten, in the numbers eleven to nineteen

analysis.evidence: In חֲמֵשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה, “fifteen years,” שָׁנָה supplies the unit for the first part of the 815 years Enosh lived after fathering Kenan.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, feminine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וּשְׁמֹנֶה מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה, the numeral counts מֵאוֹת “hundreds.” The conjunction joins these eight hundred years to the preceding fifteen years, giving 815 years.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וּ־ “and” prefixed to a feminine singular absolute cardinal numeral.
analysis.sense: eight as the multiplier of hundreds

analysis.evidence: In וּשְׁמֹנֶה מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה, שְׁמֹנֶה counts the hundreds and שָׁנָה supplies the unit, yielding “and eight hundred years.”
analysis.morphology: Cardinal numeral, plural absolute, with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: hundreds (plural מֵאוֹת, with the digits: three hundred to nine hundred)

analysis.evidence: In וּשְׁמֹנֶה מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה, the marked noun supplies the unit for “eight hundred.” Together with the preceding fifteen years, it measures the 815 years Enosh lived after fathering Kenan.
Enosh is the subject of וַיּוֹלֶד, and בָּנִים וּבָנוֹת (“sons and daughters”) are its objects. The clause says that Enosh fathered children after Kenan.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ.
